name: ZippyJSON
baseline: Foundation JSONDecoder before iOS 17 / macOS 14 (Swift wrapper over NSJSONSerialization)
verdict_reason: The 3x+ decode win was measured against the old JSONDecoder that went through NSJSONSerialization. The README now says JSONDecoder is faster than ZippyJSON on iOS 17+, so the gain only applies to apps still running on iOS 16 and earlier.
tier_reason: First-party README: the text gives only '3x+' and 'divide by 4', the per-file figures are in a chart image, and no device model, OS or Swift version is stated.
claimed_speedup: 3x+ faster decode for all 3 test files on Mac and iPhone; README rule of thumb: divide JSONDecoder's time by 4 (pre-iOS 17 only)
workload: Decoding three JSON files into Codable models (files not named in the text); release build
hardware: MacBook Pro and iPhone (models not stated)
platforms: iOS 11+, macOS 10.13+, tvOS 12+ (CocoaPods); Swift Package Manager on iOS only
one_liner: Drop-in JSONDecoder built on simdjson; 3-4x faster than the pre-iOS 17 decoder, and slower than iOS 17+'s by its own README.
how_it_is_fast: It tokenizes with simdjson, a SIMD-vectorized C++ parser, and decodes Codable values straight from the parsed result. The old Foundation decoder first built an NSDictionary/NSArray tree through NSJSONSerialization and then walked it; ZippyJSON skips that tree. ISO-8601 dates go through JJLISO8601DateFormatter instead of Foundation's formatter.
use_it_when: The app still supports iOS 16 or earlier and JSON decoding shows up in profiles on those devices
Large payloads decoded on older OS versions where the pre-2023 decoder runs
skip_it_when: Deployment target is iOS 17+ / macOS 14+: the README says the system JSONDecoder is faster
You need a faster encoder: ZippyJSON only replaces JSONDecoder
You are measuring a debug build: the README warns to build for release
caveats: Per-file numbers exist only in a chart image (misc/chart.svg); the text gives only '3x+' and 'divide by 4'.
The chart predates iOS 17; README history shows it from the 2019-2020 releases. No OS or Swift version is given.

A chart-only benchmark in the ReerJSON README (iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 26.0, by a competing library's author) shows ZippyJSON at roughly 1.0x-2.1x Foundation's decode throughput, which conflicts with ZippyJSON's own iOS 17+ note. Neither source gives text numbers for iOS 17+.
tradeoffs: Adds a C++ dependency (simdjson) and its binary size
Swift Package Manager support is iOS-only per the README

evidence.quote: JSONDecoder is faster than ZippyJSON for iOS 17+. The rest of this document describes the performance difference pre-iOS 17.
These benchmarks were done on a Macbook Pro. The results are very similar on the iPhone (ZippyJSON is 3x+ faster for all 3 files on both platforms).
divide its current time taken by 4 to approximate the time taken with ZippyJSON
